waveform.definition: The drawing of a sound's amplitude over time.

spectrogram.definition: A picture of how a sound's frequency content changes over time: time across, frequency up, level as colour.

mel-scale.definition: A frequency scale spaced as pitch is heard: roughly linear below 1 kHz and logarithmic above.

playhead.definition: The moving line that marks the current playback position.

edit-cursor.definition: The position where editing and playback start, set by clicking.

sample-rate.definition: Samples per second of a digital sound, in Hz.

bit-depth.definition: Bits per sample of a digital sound; sets its resolution.

channel.definition: One signal of a sound file; stereo has two.

mid-side.definition: Stereo written as the sum (mid) and the difference (side) of the channels.

phase.definition: Where in its cycle a wave is at a given moment.

polarity.definition: Whether a signal is upright or inverted.

level.definition: How strong a signal is, usually in dB.

gain.definition: A change of level, in dB.

true-peak.definition: The peak of the signal between samples, as a DAC would reproduce it.

loudness.definition: How loud a sound is heard, as opposed to its level.

lufs.definition: Loudness units relative to full scale (ITU-R BS.1770); 1 LU is 1 dB.

k-weighting.definition: The frequency weighting that loudness meters apply before measuring.

normalize.definition: Set a sound's peak or loudness to a target.

fade.definition: A gradual change of level at the start (fade-in) or end (fade-out).

clipping.definition: Distortion when a signal exceeds the largest value that can be stored.

dc-offset.definition: A constant shift of the signal away from zero.

noise-floor.definition: The level of the background noise under a sound.

silence.definition: A stretch with no sound above the noise floor.

cut-tail.definition: A sound that ends before its decay has died away.

take.definition: One recorded or rendered version of a sound.

render.definition: Compute a processed sound and write it as audio.

loop.definition: A sound that repeats without an audible join.

crossfade.definition: A fade-out of one sound overlapping a fade-in of another.

slice.definition: Cut a sound into parts at chosen points.

time-stretch.definition: Change a sound's duration without changing its pitch.

pitch-shift.definition: Change a sound's pitch without changing its duration.

sone.definition: The unit of loudness as heard; 1 sone is the loudness of a 1 kHz tone at 40 dB SPL.

sharpness.definition: How much a sound's energy sits at high frequencies, as heard; in acum.

roughness.definition: The rasping quality of fast amplitude modulation (about 15–300 Hz); in asper.

fluctuation-strength.definition: The sensation of slow amplitude modulation (about 1–20 Hz, strongest near 4 Hz); in vacil.

psychoacoustic-annoyance.definition: Zwicker's combination of loudness, sharpness, roughness and fluctuation strength into one annoyance value.

masking.definition: One sound making another harder or impossible to hear.

critical-band.definition: The frequency range the ear integrates as one; on the Bark scale.

curve.definition: A value drawn over time along the waveform.

overview.definition: A small picture of a whole sound used to find one's way in it.

strip.definition: The overview of one sound as Playhead draws it: waveform, curves and marks in one band.

look.definition: A named way to draw a strip, written as a short code of layers.

look-code.definition: The short text that defines a look, for example "form:overlay,shape:mirror,lane:harshness".

layer.definition: One element of a look: a waveform, spectrogram, curve, set of marks or sections.

lane.definition: A horizontal band of a strip that holds one curve.

overlay.definition: Curves drawn in one shared band instead of separate lanes.

mirrored.definition: Drawn symmetrically above and below a centre line, like a waveform.

baseline-form.definition: Drawn upwards from the bottom of the band.

horizon-chart.definition: A compact chart that folds a curve into coloured bands of increasing intensity.

sculpted-waveform.definition: A waveform whose height follows a curve, for example perceived loudness, instead of the peak level.

outline.definition: The ordinary peak waveform drawn as a thin line behind another layer.

marks.definition: Ticks along the strip at events, onsets, beats or section boundaries.

legend.definition: The text that says what each colour and line of a strip shows.

profile.definition: How much Playhead analyses: fast (curves only), sound effect, or music.

descriptor.definition: A number or curve computed from a sound that describes one of its properties.

feature.definition: A descriptor used as input to a classifier or search.

activity.definition: How much is happening: spectral change and the density of events.

arousal.definition: How exciting or calming a sound is, after the psychological dimension of the same name.

harshness.definition: How unpleasant a sound is to listen to, computed from psychoacoustic annoyance; not the same as roughness.

tension.definition: Build-up and release over time, after the model of musical tension by Farbood (2012).

harmonic-tension.definition: How far the harmony is from rest, from the tonal interval space.

novelty.definition: How much a moment differs from what came before.

spectral-surprise.definition: Change of the spectrum that loudness does not explain.

surprisal.definition: Information content of an event: the less expected, the higher.

structural-change.definition: Where a piece moves to a new part, signed: up where sound enters, down where it falls away or breaks off.

local-pulse.definition: How clearly a regular pulse is felt at each moment.

onset.definition: The moment a sound or note begins.

onset-strength.definition: How strongly new sound arrives at each moment; peaks are hits.

event.definition: One distinct sound within a file, such as a hit, a step or a creak, with a start and an end.

attack.definition: The first part of a sound, from its start to its peak.

body.definition: The sustained, often tonal, part of a sound after its attack.

decay.definition: The part of a sound in which it dies away.

tail.definition: The late part of a decay, including reverberation.

transient.definition: A short, fast change of level and spectrum, typically at an attack.

beat.definition: The regular pulse a listener taps along to.

downbeat.definition: The first beat of a bar.

bar.definition: A group of beats, usually four.

tempo.definition: The speed of the beat, in beats per minute (BPM).

section.definition: A part of a piece, such as an intro or chorus, found from where its sound changes.

recurrence.definition: How much a sound returns to states it has been in before.

repetition-rate.definition: How often a pattern repeats, in Hz.

periodicity.definition: How strongly a sound is periodic (pitched) rather than noisy.

phase-coherence.definition: How steadily a sound's phases advance; 1 for a steady tone, near 0 for noise.

time-arrow.definition: How much a sound changes when played backwards; high for hits that decay.

impulsiveness.definition: How much a sound consists of clicks, cracks and crackle, from spectral kurtosis.

spectral-kurtosis.definition: A statistic that is 0 for steady noise, −1 for a steady tone and large for clicks.

spectral-motion.definition: How fast the spectrum's centre moves up or down, in octaves per second.

spectral-centroid.definition: The centre of mass of a spectrum; a measure of brightness.

reshaping.definition: Spectral change that does not move the centre, as when a spectrum spreads or narrows.

burstiness.definition: Whether events come regularly (below 0), at random (0) or in bursts (above 0).

temporal-entropy.definition: How evenly a sound's energy is spread over time.

decay-time.definition: The time a sound takes to fall by 60 dB.

damping.definition: How quickly a vibrating body loses energy.

material.definition: What an impacted object is made of, as heard: damped, glass-like or metal-like.

partial.definition: One frequency component of a sound.

overtone.definition: A partial above the lowest one.

inharmonic.definition: With partials that are not whole-number multiples of a fundamental, as in bells and struck metal.

quality-checks.definition: Automatic checks for clipping, DC offset, silence and cut tails.

self-check.definition: A test that edits a sound in a known way and checks that the analysis changes as it must.

de-harsh.definition: A tool that turns down resonances only while the sound is harsh.

attack-and-body.definition: A tool that splits a sound into its transient part and its sustained part, to rebalance them.

layer-remix.definition: A tool that separates a sound into layers and mixes them again at new levels.

tension-shaper.definition: A tool that turns the tension curve into gain and brightness automation.

loop-maker.definition: A tool that finds and crossfades loop points where the sound repeats best.

variations.definition: Several slightly different versions of one sound, to avoid repetition in games.

clean-up.definition: A tool that repairs what the quality checks flag before a sound is exported.

reverb-on-tails.definition: Reverberation fed only from the decays of the events, keeping the attacks dry.

drive-hits.definition: Saturation applied only to the events' attacks or bodies.

ring-time.definition: A tool that lengthens or shortens how long each event rings after its peak.

level-events.definition: A tool that evens out how loud the events are, one gain per event, without touching their shape.

fold-to-mono.definition: Turn stereo into mono with the channels' phase lined up, so nothing cancels.

widen-tails.definition: Make or widen stereo only after the attacks, keeping attacks centred and the result mono-compatible.

mono-compatibility.definition: How well a stereo sound survives being summed to mono.

decorrelation.definition: Making two signals less alike while keeping their spectrum, to widen a stereo image.

comb-filtering.definition: Regular notches in a spectrum when a signal is summed with a delayed copy of itself.

cancellation.definition: Loss of level when signals of opposite phase are summed.

pre-echo.definition: A faint smear of a sound before its attack, caused by frame-based processing.

eq.definition: An equaliser: a filter that changes the level of frequency bands.

dynamic-eq.definition: An EQ whose band gains follow the level in each band.

automation.definition: Parameter changes over time, recorded or drawn.

compressor.definition: A processor that turns loud passages down by a ratio above a threshold.

threshold.definition: The level above which a processor acts.

ratio.definition: How strongly a compressor turns the level down above its threshold.

attack-time.definition: How fast a processor reacts when the level rises.

release-time.definition: How fast a processor recovers when the level falls.

gate.definition: A processor or condition that opens only above a threshold.

saturation.definition: Soft distortion that adds harmonics and rounds peaks.

pumping.definition: Audible rise and fall of the background caused by a compressor.

evenness.definition: How alike the events are in loudness.

effect-chain.definition: Effects applied one after another to a sound.

morph.definition: A gradual blend from one sound into another.

cross-synthesis.definition: Combining the spectrum of one sound with the envelope or excitation of another.

convolution.definition: Filtering one sound by another, for example by a room's impulse response.

envelope-transfer.definition: Giving one sound the level envelope of another.

ring-modulation.definition: Multiplying two signals, which creates sum and difference frequencies.

granular.definition: Built from many short grains of sound.

accent.definition: A short added sound placed at a moment of another sound to emphasise it.

generator.definition: A part of the app that makes new sounds from parameters.

synth.definition: A sound generator built from oscillators, noise, envelopes and filters.

impact-model.definition: A physical model of a struck object of a given material and shape.

resynthesis.definition: Rebuilding a sound from parameters measured on it, such as its partials and decays.

modal.definition: Made of resonant modes, each with a frequency and a decay.

texture.definition: A continuous sound made of many small events, such as rain, fire or gravel.

reaction.definition: A generator in which an action, such as an object moving or a force, drives the sound of a medium that responds to it (gravel, water, air).

medium.definition: What reacts to an action: gravel, leaves, water, air, sparks or a force field.

drive-curve.definition: A curve that controls a sound's parameters over time.

inertia.definition: How slowly a reaction settles after the action stops.

foley.definition: Everyday sounds performed and recorded in sync with picture.

ambience.definition: The background sound of a place.

one-shot.definition: A short sound played once, such as a hit or a UI click.

whoosh.definition: The sound of something moving fast past the listener.

finishing.definition: The last steps before export: format, channels, fades and level.

bar-shape.definition: A long solid body, such as a rod or beam.

membrane.definition: A stretched skin, as on a drum.

shell.definition: A thin curved body, such as a can or pot.

wire.definition: A stiff string or wire that rings with slightly stretched (inharmonic) partials.

box.definition: A hollow body with flat sides.

track.definition: A row of a DAW session that holds clips on the timeline and has its own mixer channel.

folder-track.definition: A track that holds other tracks: it sums their sound and can show them as one.

clip.definition: One piece of audio or MIDI on a track, placed at a point in time.

session.definition: All of one piece of DAW work: its tracks, clips, routing and settings; also called a project.

timeline.definition: The time axis of a session, along which clips are placed.

marker.definition: A named point in time stored in a session or a sound file (a cue in a WAV file).

region.definition: A named span of time with a start and an end, stored in a session or a sound file.

snap.definition: Making a clip or an edit jump to the nearest grid line, marker, clip edge or onset while it is moved.

mute.definition: Silencing a track without removing it; the button is often labelled M.

solo.definition: Hearing only the soloed tracks; the button is often labelled S.

fader.definition: The level control of a mixer channel.

pan.definition: Where a sound sits between left and right; also the control that sets it.

bus.definition: A mixer channel that sums the signals sent to it, so they can be processed together (a drum bus, a reverb bus).

master-bus.definition: The bus everything is summed into before the output: what is rendered as the mix.

send.definition: A copy of a track's signal sent to a bus at its own level, while the track keeps playing.

insert.definition: An effect in a channel's own signal path, which all of the signal passes through.

routing.definition: How signals travel between tracks, buses, sends and outputs.

mix.definition: The sum of all tracks as it is heard; also the work of balancing them.

stem.definition: A submix of related tracks (drums, dialogue, music) rendered to its own file, so the parts can be mixed or delivered separately.

zero-crossing.definition: A point where the waveform crosses zero; cuts and loop points made there do not click.

headroom.definition: The distance in dB between the highest level a signal reaches and the level where it would clip.

dynamic-range.definition: The span in dB between a sound's loud and quiet parts, or between the highest level a system takes and its noise floor.

loudness-range.definition: How much the loudness of a programme varies, in LU: the span between the 10th and 95th percentile of its short-term loudness.

integrated-loudness.definition: The loudness of a whole programme, with silence and quiet passages gated out, in LUFS.

short-term-loudness.definition: Loudness over a sliding 3 s window, in LUFS.

momentary-loudness.definition: Loudness over a sliding 400 ms window, in LUFS.

loudness-target.definition: The integrated loudness a programme is delivered or played at, such as −23 LUFS for EBU R 128 broadcast or about −14 LUFS on streaming services.

loudness-matching.definition: Bringing two versions to the same loudness before comparing them, so that the louder one does not seem better only because it is louder.

ab-comparison.definition: Switching between two versions, ideally at matched loudness, to hear which is better.

reference-track.definition: A finished recording played for comparison while mixing or mastering.

crest-factor.definition: The ratio of peak to RMS level, in dB: high for punchy, dynamic sound, low for dense, compressed sound.

rms-level.definition: The root mean square of a signal over a window: its average power, as a level.

stereo-width.definition: How different the two channels are, from mono (not at all) to wide.

envelope.definition: How a quantity, usually level, changes over the course of a sound; also a drawn curve that controls a parameter.

frequency-band.definition: A range of frequencies measured or processed together: an EQ band, a critical band, a mel band.

high-pass-filter.definition: A filter that passes the frequencies above its cutoff and attenuates those below.

low-pass-filter.definition: A filter that passes the frequencies below its cutoff and attenuates those above.

limiter.definition: A compressor with a very high ratio and a fast attack that keeps the level below a ceiling.

multiband-compressor.definition: A compressor that works on several frequency bands separately.

transient-shaper.definition: A processor that raises or lowers the attack and the sustain of sounds independently of their level.

sidechain.definition: A second input through which another signal controls a processor, as when music is turned down under dialogue.

ducking.definition: Turning one sound down automatically while another plays, usually with a sidechained compressor.

reverb.definition: The dense reflections of a sound in a space, or an effect that imitates them.

delay.definition: An effect that plays the sound again after a set time, often repeating and fading (echo).

dither.definition: Low-level noise added when the bit depth is reduced, so that the rounding error becomes noise instead of distortion.

mastering.definition: The last stage before release: the final EQ, dynamics and loudness of a mix, and checks for the delivery format.

drop.definition: The moment in a dance track when the full beat and bass come in, usually after a build-up or a breakdown.

build-up.definition: A passage that raises tension towards a drop: rising pitch, filter sweeps, faster rolls, a riser.

breakdown.definition: A passage where the beat and bass fall away, leaving pads, chords or vocals.

riser.definition: A sound that rises in pitch, brightness or level to lead into a drop or a transition.

sweep.definition: A glide through a range of frequencies: a tone or noise whose pitch or brightness moves, or a filter swept across the spectrum.

cue-point.definition: A stored position in a track that a DJ or a player jumps to or starts from.

beatgrid.definition: The beats and bars of a track as a grid, used to sync, loop and jump in time.

beatmatching.definition: Bringing two tracks to the same tempo with their beats aligned.

phrase.definition: A run of bars, usually 8, 16 or 32 in dance music, that forms one musical unit; DJs mix at phrase boundaries.

key.definition: The tonal centre and scale of a piece, such as A minor; DJs mix tracks in compatible keys (harmonic mixing).
